quickAnswer: International degree and exchange students enrolled at accredited Turkish universities apply for a Student Residence Permit (Articles 38–41 of Law No. 6458) via e-Ikamet and typically submit paper dossiers through their university's international office. Students may opt into public SGK insurance within three months of enrollment, and degree students can work legally with a Ministry work permit.

body.text: At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders arrange client-paid, flat-fee scouting trips, campus-area orientation, and independent local introductions in Istanbul, Ankara, and beyond. Paid by our clients and independent of provider commissions, we do not file immigration applications, review student leases, or offer legal advice—those responsibilities belong to licensed Turkish attorneys, university international offices, and the Presidency of Migration Management (Göç İdaresi).
How do exchange and degree students apply for Student Ikamet via university offices?

Students first complete their online application on the [e-Residence (e-Ikamet) portal](https://e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr/) while still within their legal visa or visa-free window. Under the protocol between higher education institutions and Göç İdaresi, most universities in Istanbul and Ankara collect signed student dossiers at their International Students Office and forward them directly to the provincial migration directorate.

According to a March 2026 [Presidency of Migration Management announcement](https://en.goc.gov.tr/the-presidency-of-migration-management-met-with-international-students-at-an-iftar-dinner), international students receive a Foreigner ID Number (YKN) during university enrollment so they can open bank accounts and register addresses early. Permits are issued for the length of the degree program (provided passport validity extends 60 days beyond the permit), and graduates can apply within six months for a one-year post-graduation short-term permit.
Before visiting your campus international office, assemble these core documents listed on [e-Ikamet Required Documents](https://e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr/Ikamet/IstenenBelgeler):

items: Signed e-Ikamet form: Printed application form generated after online submission.
Active student certificate (Öğrenci Belgesi): Issued by your university registrar confirming formal enrollment or Erasmus/exchange placement.
Passport and biometric photos: Original passport, copies of photo and entry-stamp pages, plus four biometric photos.
Address verification: University dormitory letter, notarized lease, or notarized host undertaking.
Card fee receipt: Payment proof for the annual valuable-paper card fee published on [Göç İdaresi Fee Amounts](https://en.goc.gov.tr/documents-for-residence-permit-fee-amount).

body.text: What health insurance (SGK vs private) is required for students?

Foreign university students can apply for Türkiye's public General Health Insurance (GSS) through the Social Security Institution (SGK) within three months of their initial university registration date. Under [Göç İdaresi Residence Permit Types](https://en.goc.gov.tr/residence-permit-types), students who miss that three-month window lose eligibility for student GSS and must carry Turkish private health insurance for their permit's duration.

Public SGK student coverage grants access to state hospitals and subsidized prescriptions nationwide, whereas basic Ikamet-compliant private policies mainly satisfy immigration requirements with narrower outpatient caps. Whichever option you choose, the policy dates must cover your entire requested permit period without gaps.
Can foreign students work part-time legally?

Yes, but never on a Student Residence Permit alone. Under Article 41 of Law No. 6458 and Article 19 of International Workforce Law No. 6735, formal associate, bachelor's, master's, and doctoral students may work legally only after their employer obtains a work permit from the Ministry of Labour and Social Security.

The rules differ sharply by degree level, as outlined by [Göç İdaresi Work Permit guidance](https://en.goc.gov.tr/work-permit) and the [METU International Students Office](https://iso.metu.edu.tr/en/work-permits): associate and undergraduate students may only apply after completing their first academic year and are limited to part-time contracts under Turkish Labour Law No. 4857. Master's and PhD students are exempt from both the first-year waiting period and the part-time restriction. Obtaining a student work permit does not cancel your underlying student Ikamet.
Which student-friendly neighborhoods have safe transit?

Choosing a neighborhood near rail lines saves hours of daily traffic in both cities. In Istanbul, Beşiktaş, Kadıköy (Moda and Caferağa), and Sarıyer (near Hacıosman M2 Metro) connect directly to Boğaziçi, İTÜ, Koç, and Marmara campuses. In Ankara, Çankaya (Bahçelievler, Ayrancı, and Yüzüncü Yıl) puts METU, Bilkent, and Hacettepe students along M1/M2 metro and Ankaray corridors.

faq.q: Do Erasmus and short-term exchange students need a Student Residence Permit?
faq.a: Yes, if your exchange program lasts longer than 90 days (or exceeds your visa exemption), you must apply on e-Ikamet and submit documents through your host university's international office.

faq.q: How long is a Turkish Student Residence Permit valid?
faq.a: For degree students, permits generally cover the full length of the study program—for example, four years for an undergraduate degree—provided your passport validity exceeds that period by 60 days.

faq.q: Can I work during my first year as an undergraduate student in Türkiye?
faq.a: No. Associate and bachelor's students must complete their first academic year before an employer can apply for a part-time work permit with the Ministry of Labour and Social Security.

faq.q: What happens if I miss the 3-month SGK health insurance deadline?
faq.a: Under [Göç İdaresi rules](https://en.goc.gov.tr/residence-permit-types), missing the three-month window from initial registration forfeits the student GSS option, requiring you to purchase compliant private health insurance instead.

faq.q: Do student residence permit years count toward 8-year permanent residence?
faq.a: Yes, but at half value: every two years held on a student Ikamet counts as one year toward the eight-year permanent residence threshold.

faq.q: Can Itinerary of Türkiye secure university admission or file my Student Ikamet?
faq.a: No. [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/) provides independent scouting trips, city orientation, and vetted introductions; university offices, licensed attorneys, and Göç İdaresi manage admissions and permits.
